name: FLUX.2 dev (fp8mixed)
desc: The third engine. Photoreal and general work driven by full natural sentences. Its edge is not prettiness - it is LITERALISM: it does what the sentence says about layout, camera, count and colour. Installed since July, unreachable from the app until now.
prompt_style: complete natural sentences, or the official FLUX.2 JSON prompt object. Not tags.
note: THE cfg 4.0 ABOVE IS NOT A cfg. There is no KSampler in this graph. It is the FluxGuidance value on node 7 of 40_flux2_t2i.json and it behaves nothing like SDXL cfg: swept 2.0 / 2.5 / 4.0 / 6.0 / 8.0 at one seed it never rerolled the composition and never burned out - it moved contrast and adherence smoothly, and 8.0 is still a usable frame where SDXL at cfg 8 would be fried. There is also NO NEGATIVE PROMPT and none can be added: BasicGuider takes a single conditioning. Write negation as a positive fact. steps 8 is the Turbo path that 40_flux2_t2i.json ships wired; steps_quality 20 is the same graph with the Turbo LoRA bypassed. They are two different pictures at one seed, not two qualities of one picture - see turbo below before assuming 20 is simply better.

turbo.measured: 1024 square, seed 5150, one prompt: Turbo 8 steps 9.0 s, no Turbo 20 steps 19.7 s, no Turbo 28 steps 24.1 s. 2.2x, not the 6x the folklore implies.
turbo.verdict: IT IS NOT THE SAME PICTURE. At a fixed seed Turbo composes a DIFFERENT FRAME, so it cannot be used to preview a no-Turbo render, only to explore. What it actually costs, rendered four subjects side by side at one seed (samples/flux2/turbo): MECHANISM, and only mechanism. On a watch movement the 20-step path drew real gear teeth, jewel screws, a click and ratchet and a blued spring; the Turbo path drew plausible-at-a-glance gears with mushy teeth. In-image text survived Turbo perfectly. A crowd scene survived. And on a face Turbo was arguably BETTER - grittier, more of the pores and fine lines the prompt asked for, where the 20-step render smoothed her toward a stock portrait.
turbo.rule: Turbo for faces, crowds, text, layout tests and contact sheets. Drop it for anything with visible machinery, type-as-object or fine repeating structure. Below 6 steps Turbo goes soft; 4 steps is not shippable.
turbo.counterpoint: This contradicts the survey claim that FLUX.2 dev without Turbo takes 20+ minutes per image. On this box it takes 20 seconds. Whatever that reviewer measured, it was not this configuration.

measured.fits: YES. No OOM at any size tried. ComfyUI logs 'Model Flux2 prepared for dynamic VRAM loading. 33813MB Staged.' and streams it - a 33.8 GB transformer plus an 8.3 GB text encoder running on a 32 GB card. Peak nvidia-smi during a render: 28.3 GB.
measured.prompt_change_cost: ~4.5 s. Re-encoding a NEW prompt through Mistral-3 costs about what four sampler steps cost, and it is not cached. A sweep that varies only the seed is materially cheaper per image than a sweep that varies the prompt - the opposite of the SDXL habit.
measured.timing_resolution: +/-1.5 s. comfy.py polls the queue on a 1.5 s tick, so the wall clocks in the ledger are quantised. Differences under 2 s mean nothing.
measured.composition_holds_to: 2.4 MP. One prompt, one seed, six sizes: 1536x1536 and 2048x1152 both came back single-subject and coherent. Qwen-Image duplicates composition past about 2 MP. FLUX.2 did not, at either size.
measured.hex_colour_accuracy: Asked for a background of exactly #12303F and a circle of exactly #E8B04B. Got #102643 and #EEB650, sampled off the PNG. Within about 4% per channel. No other engine on this box takes a hex code at all.
measured.face_pixels: PARTIAL RESULT, READ THE CAVEAT. Rendered the same full-body prompt and seed at 832x1216, 1024x1536, 1152x1728 and 1280x1920 (samples/flux2/face). The face resolves properly from 1152x1728 up and reproduces the project's known ~90 px mush at 832x1216. BUT FLUX.2 REFRAMED at each size rather than holding the shot, so this is not a controlled pixels-per-face measurement and must not be quoted as one. What it does establish: rendering bigger is cheap here (1280x1920 cost about the same as 1536x1536, roughly 20 s) and nothing broke at any of those sizes.
measured.contamination_note: Three numbers in the ledger are NOT FLUX.2 measurements: settings/noturbo_s20_g6.0 at 168.8 s, and the ab cells hands_tool__qwen at 839.6 s and the ab batch total. Another agent's HunyuanVideo jobs took the queue at ~13 minutes each and evicted the model. Cold reload after a foreign model family costs 60-150 s. Everything else in the table is warm and contiguous. This is also why flux2_probe.py grew a --batch flag.

vs_qwen.how: Six prompts plus one anime prompt, identical text, identical seed 5150, identical frame size, each engine at its own recommended settings (FLUX.2 Turbo 8 steps guidance 4.0; Qwen-Image 2512 20 steps cfg 2.5 with its template negative). Pairs are in samples/flux2/ab/ and tiled in _sheet_ab.jpg.

flux2_wins.instruction_follow: DECISIVE. 'Shot straight down from above. Exactly three green apples in a row on the left half. A single white enamel jug on the right half. A wooden spoon between them running top edge to bottom edge. Nothing else on the table.' FLUX.2 got all five. Qwen ignored the camera angle entirely and shot it from three-quarters. If the shot description is load-bearing, this is the engine.
flux2_wins.multi_subject: Three people, three costumes, three actions, three positions. Both engines attributed correctly, but FLUX.2 spaced them evenly across the frame as asked while Qwen clustered them centre-right and overlapped two of them. Composition instructions land on FLUX.2 and drift on Qwen.
flux2_wins.structured_json: BFL's JSON prompt object, fed verbatim, honoured subject placement, action, lens and composition. Qwen has no equivalent input.
flux2_wins.hex_colour: Only engine here that takes one.
flux2_wins.anime: Both produced genuine cel-shaded anime - see the correction below - but FLUX.2's line art and character proportions read more authentically animated.

qwen_wins.portrait_skin: CLEARLY, AND IT IS THE SAME LITERALISM BACKWARDS. The prompt said 'broken capillaries across the cheeks'. FLUX.2 drew literal red vein lines across the face and disfigured her. Qwen produced a believable weathered fisherman. FLUX.2 renders the noun you wrote; if the noun is a medical term you get a diagram.
qwen_wins.hands: Split, not a FLUX win. FLUX.2 nailed a fly-tying close-up - ten distinct fingers, correct joints, the scraped knuckle that was asked for. On dough-kneading at the same seed it produced a tangle with extra digits; Qwen's was clean. Hands are good on FLUX.2, not reliable.
qwen_wins.illustration: Watercolour is Qwen's, and not close. Qwen gave pigment pooling, wash bleed, drips down the paper and real cold-press texture. FLUX.2 gave a clean digital rendering of a fox that happens to be pale. Anything hand-media stays off FLUX.2.

ties.in_image_text: THIS OVERTURNS A STANDING PROJECT ASSUMPTION. 'Qwen owns text, FLUX.2 is weaker' is what 22-flux2/README.md and the capability card say. Rendered head to head, both wrote NORTHWIND SUPPLY CO. / EST 1904 letter-perfect. FLUX.2 also rendered two handwritten index cards - 'TUESDAY: FEED THE CHICKENS' and 'BUY NAILS' - correctly first try, and text survived the Turbo LoRA intact. Qwen was marginally more faithful to the exact string (it omitted the full stop after EST, as written; FLUX.2 added one). Treat text as a tie and route on the rest of the shot.

vs_qwen.correction: The project rule 'Qwen cannot be steered off photography by prompt at any cfg' did NOT hold in this test. At 20 steps and cfg 2.5, given a prompt whose medium is stated as NOUNS - 'cel-shaded anime illustration', 'hand-painted 1990s animation background', 'flat colour fills', 'clean black line art' - Qwen returned a genuine anime frame. The earlier finding was measured at cfg 1.0 with the Lightning LoRA. Worth a proper re-test before the rule is quoted again.

director_verdict: Route to FLUX.2 when the SHOT DESCRIPTION is the work: a specified camera angle, a specified layout, a stated count of things, several people who must each do a different thing, a named hex colour, or type that has to be readable. Route to Qwen when the SURFACE is the work: skin, weather, hand-media, anything where you want the model to interpolate a plausible photograph rather than execute your sentence. Keep Animagine for danbooru-tag anime and for anything a LoRA has to attach to - no LoRA on this box fits FLUX.2 except the Turbo distill. The one-line rule: FLUX.2 obeys, Qwen imagines.
strong: Camera, layout and count instructions - the strongest on this box by a distance
In-image text, including handwriting (tied with Qwen, better than believed)
Named hex colours, within ~4% per channel
Mechanism and fine repeating structure at 20 steps without Turbo
Coherent to 2.4 MP where Qwen duplicates past 2 MP
Competent cel-shaded anime without a LoRA
weak: Literalism cuts both ways: a technical noun gets drawn as a diagram ('broken capillaries' became red lines on a face).
Hands are good but not reliable - one clean render and one tangle in the same session.
Watercolour and hand-media are clean and digital. Qwen and Animagine both beat it.
The Turbo path degrades mechanism specifically.
No negative prompt at all, so every SDXL-era suppression habit has to be rewritten.
No LoRA on this box attaches to it except the Turbo distill. It is a standalone aesthetic, not a base to build on.
Cannot co-reside with Qwen-Image or HunyuanVideo. On a shared box an interleaved foreign job costs a 60-150 s reload. Batch by model, and use flux2_probe.py --batch.

do: Write complete sentences. Subject, then what it is doing, then the setting, then the light, then the lens and aperture, then the finish.
State negation positively: 'a plain white wall behind her', 'both hands empty', 'nothing else on the table'.
Say the camera angle out loud. 'Shot straight down from above' is honoured here and ignored by Qwen.
Give counts as digits-in-words: 'exactly three green apples in a row'.
Quote text and say 'reads exactly'. It lands, with or without Turbo.
Give hex codes when colour matters.
For multi-character shots, give each person a position in the frame and an action in the same clause.
The JSON prompt object is a first-class input, not a trick.
dont: Danbooru tags. This is not a CLIP.
'masterpiece, best quality, absurdres'. quality_tags is empty on purpose, exactly as on the Qwen card.
Clinical or technical nouns for skin and body unless you want them drawn literally.
Adjective moods. The FLUX.2 JSON schema has a 'mood' field and it is the same trap as everywhere else on this box - the model renders nouns, not adjectives. Keep every JSON value a noun phrase.
Anything in a negative field. There is no negative field.

samples: studio/samples/flux2/ - settings/ (13-cell step and guidance sweep), size/ (6-size resolution ladder), spread/ (12 subjects), turbo/ (4 subjects x Turbo on/off), face/ (one full-body prompt at four frame sizes), ab/ (7 prompts x 2 engines at matched seed and size). Tiled for looking at as _sheet_*.jpg in the same folder. Every render is a row in _measured.json.
tool: studio/_tools/flux2_probe.py --mode settings|size|spread|turbo|face|ab|one  [--batch when the box is busy]
